_comment: Security test matrix for DummyJSON API. Each entry defines a scenario the matrix runner will execute. 'expectedStatus' is the production-secure expectation. 'observedStatus' is what DummyJSON actually returns (documented after running). 'securityClassification' distinguishes contract behaviour from security hypothesis.

scenarios.description: Valid credentials return access token and refresh token
Invalid password returns 400 and does not reveal whether username exists
Empty credentials return 400
GET /auth/me with valid token returns current user profile
GET /auth/me without token returns 401
GET /auth/me with a malformed token returns 401
POST /auth/refresh with valid refresh token returns new tokens
POST /auth/refresh with invalid refresh token is safely rejected [DummyJSON returns 403; 401 would be more precise]
scenarios.securityHypothesis: Both 401 and 403 correctly reject an invalid refresh token. 401 is semantically more precise (unrecognisable credential); 403 is defensible. Low-severity observation, not a vulnerability.

scenarios.description: Admin can read all users via GET /users
Regular user can read all users via GET /users [HYPOTHESIS: should be restricted or return filtered data in production]
scenarios.securityHypothesis: In a production system, non-admin users should not have access to the full user directory. DummyJSON allows this as it is a public sandbox.

scenarios.description: Unauthenticated request to GET /users returns data [FINDING: no auth enforced]
scenarios.securityHypothesis: Public user directory without any authentication is a data exposure risk. All user PII including SSN, bank details and passwords are accessible without credentials.

scenarios.description: Regular user attempts to delete another user via DELETE /users/{id} — must return 403 [DummyJSON returns 200: FINDING]
scenarios.securityHypothesis: Non-admin users must not be able to delete other users. DummyJSON does not enforce role or ownership checks on DELETE /users/{id} — any authenticated user can delete any user record. This is a critical BFLA (Broken Function Level Authorization) vulnerability.

scenarios.description: Unauthenticated DELETE /users/{id} [FINDING: no auth enforced on destructive operations]
scenarios.securityHypothesis: Destructive operations must require authentication. DummyJSON simulates delete without enforcing auth.

scenarios.description: Unauthenticated POST /products/add [FINDING: write operation requires no auth]
scenarios.securityHypothesis: Resource creation should require authentication. DummyJSON accepts unauthenticated POST to /products/add.

scenarios.description: User can read their own cart via GET /carts/user/{ownId}
User reads another user's cart via GET /carts/user/{otherId} [FINDING: no ownership check]
scenarios.securityHypothesis: A user should only be able to read their own cart. DummyJSON does not enforce ownership on /carts/user/{id}.

scenarios.description: User reads another user's todos via GET /users/{otherId}/todos [FINDING: no ownership check]
scenarios.securityHypothesis: A user's todos are private resources. Cross-user access should require elevated role.

scenarios.description: User updates another user's record via PUT /users/{otherId} [FINDING: no ownership/role check]
scenarios.securityHypothesis: Users should not be able to modify other users' records. Only admin should have this permission.

scenarios.description: GET /users/{id} response contains plaintext password field [CRITICAL FINDING]
scenarios.securityHypothesis: User records must never expose passwords in any form. SSN, bank card numbers and IBAN are PCI/PII data that should be masked or omitted from API responses.

scenarios.description: Login response does not expose password in body
GET /users/999999 returns 404 for non-existent user
GET /users/abc returns 400 for non-numeric ID
POST /auth/login with SQL injection payload returns 400 without stack trace
GET /users/0 returns 400 or 404 — ID 0 is not a valid user
GET /users/-1 must return 400 for invalid negative ID [DummyJSON returns 404: minor contract gap]
scenarios.securityHypothesis: A negative integer is not a valid user ID format. The server should return 400 (Bad Request) to signal invalid input. DummyJSON returns 404 (Not Found) — treating it as a valid-but-missing ID rather than rejecting the malformed input at the validation layer.

scenarios.description: GET /users/{id} response matches expected user schema
POST /auth/login response matches LoginResponse schema
GET /products response matches ProductsList schema
GET /carts/{id} response matches Cart schema
